text:
maria: Heads-up — after last night's kernel-fanout change I see a ~12-18% p99 latency increase on the large-chat workload. Traces look concentrated around the paged-attn path choosing the flashv2 variant less often than before.

infra-bot: deploy redwood/serving-runtime@v4.12.0 completed by ci-deploy (2351231200).

aj: Can you paste the reproducer and the exact numbers you saw? Is this isolated to one model/sequence-length distribution?

maria: Quick repro (synthetic convo load):
```
# run from perfbox
./bench_load --model rwinf-13b --seq 2048 --concurrency 12 --duration 300
```
Baseline (pre-fanout): p50=78ms p95=210ms p99=310ms tps=320
After fanout: p50=80ms p95=240ms p99=365ms tps=290
Also saw more variance in CPU on the host handling pagewalks.

sasha: The kernel selection tweak in the patch changed the threshold logic in batch-sampler. We now pick flashv2 when `seq_len > 1536 && avg_bucket_width > 512` — previously it was `> 1024`. Small shift but can alter routing for the long-tails. Snippet: 
```
if (seq_len > KERNEL_THRESHOLD && bucket_w > BUCKET_MIN) select(FLASHV2)
else select(FUSED_ATTEN)
```

dmitri: Telemetry that correlates: kv_residency dropped from ~0.92 to ~0.6 for the long-tail cohort after deploy. pagewalks/sec jumped ~3x. Sample trace excerpt from the pager: 
```
[2026-03-17T23:12:03Z] pagewalk: shard=13 page_miss=1 kv_fetch_ms=4.8
[2026-03-17T23:12:04Z] pagewalk: shard=13 page_miss=1 kv_fetch_ms=5.1
```
Lower residency -> more remote KV fetches -> more latency variance and less benefit from flashv2 fusion (because fusion expects contiguous KV residency).

ben: Two quick experiments we can run: 1) revert the kernel-threshold change on a 10% canary and measure p99; 2) adjust batch-sampler to prefer fused-attn for any seq_len in [1024,1792] when kv_residency < 0.75. Option 2 is cheaper and doesn't require full rollback.

maria: I sketched a small patch for option 2 (fallback by kv_residency):
```
// pseudo
if (kv_residency < 0.75 && seq_len >= 1024 && seq_len <= 1792) {
  prefer(FUSED_ATTEN);
} else {
  apply_existing_kernel_policy();
}
```
I'd like to run canary (10%) with that policy and also a reduced micro-batch cap (max_micro=8) to see batching impact.

aj: I can schedule the canary on canary-pool-2. Steps: a) deploy kernel-policy change as feature-flag, b) enable flag for 10% routing, c) run synthetic load plus beta production traffic for 30m, d) collect p50/p95/p99 + kv_residency + pagewalks. I can start at 00:30 UTC.

sasha: Also add a short profiler run to capture kernel selection counts and backend time split (KV fetch vs compute). If we see compute drop but kv wait rise, it's definitely residency. We should record `kernel_choice_histogram` and `kv_wait_ms` for canary.

dmitri: Agreed. I'll add a temporary metric: `kv_residency_cohort` and log per-request pagewalks. If we confirm drop, we need to revisit the paging allocation heuristics — likely the recent slab reshuffle reduced hot-page locality for long convos.

ben: One more note: if fused-attn is faster for mid-lengths when KV is fragmented, we should add an automated fallback in the runtime: fallback to fused if kv_residency < X and p99 delta > Y over sampling window. That gives graceful degradation when paging degrades.

maria: Perfect. Action items: aj will run canary with the feature-flag patch (kv-based fallback + max_micro=8), sasha will collect kernel selection + kv_wait profiles, dmitri will surface pagewalk logs and residency cohorts, ben and I will watch the metrics and decide rollback if p99 stays +10% after 30m.

infra-bot: canary scheduled: redwood/serving-runtime@v4.12.1-feature-kv-fallback -> canary-pool-2 at 2026-03-18T00:30:00Z by aj.

maria: Thanks — ping here once the 30m run finishes with metrics.
